claim.quote: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.46 ppm

key_value_text.quote: The anomaly value is 116,592,040(54)x10^-11 with 0.46 ppm precision.

name: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.46 ppm

significance.quote: 3.3 standard deviations greater than the standard model prediction
significance.value: 3.3 standard deviations greater than the standard model prediction (combined with BNL E821: 4.2 standard deviations)

summary.plain: Fermilab's first result: the most precise measurement yet of a subtle property of the muon, agreeing with an earlier Brookhaven measurement and together pointing to a possible gap in our understanding of particle physics.
summary.technical: First Fermilab (E989) measurement of a_mu, combining Run-1 data with the BNL E821 result to a combined a_mu = 116,592,061(41)x10^-11, 4.2 sigma above the (2020 consensus) Standard Model prediction, per the paper's own reported significance.

title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.46 ppm
why_it_matters: The muon's anomalous magnetic moment is one of the most precisely predicted and measured quantities in physics; a persistent discrepancy between measurement and Standard Model prediction would be evidence of undiscovered particles or forces.
